title: Foundations: Timber and Joinery Processes
welcome_lead: Enter the wood workshop and pick up the saw, plane and chisel that shape every timber product.
meta_desc: Learn timber sawing, planing and traditional joints for GCSE Design & Technology.
final_note: You can name the right tool or joint for a timber project.

walkthroughs.body_html: Joinery begins with careful marking using a try square, marking gauge and pencil. A tenon saw handles fine cross-cuts; a rip saw follows the grain. A plane removes shavings to leave a flat, square edge ready for joining.
A butt joint is fast but weak. A dowel joint adds hidden strength. A mortise and tenon is the classic strong frame joint, while a finger joint gives maximum glue area for boxes.

walkthroughs.h2: Picking a joint for a chair
walkthroughs.body_html: A wooden dining chair leg must resist racking forces. A mortise and tenon between leg and rail is the standard choice because the long glue surfaces and tight fit resist twisting under load.

mcqs.q: What determines whether a timber is a hardwood or softwood?
options: How long the tree took to grow.
The black colour absorbing energy.
Whether the wood itself is physically hard or soft.
The type of tree - deciduous (hardwood) or coniferous (softwood), not its hardness.

mcqs.q: Why is injection moulding suited to high-volume production?
options: The black colour absorbing energy.
It is the cheapest method for any quantity.
Tooling cost is high but per-unit cost is very low at scale.
It is the only way to make plastic items.
